angle: Stop buying GPUs to fix I/O problems—optimize data movement to cut latency and cost.
sourceTitle: Architecting memory and storage in the AI era
linkedinPost:
Your GPU bill is loud. Your data pipeline is the real bottleneck.

MIT Technology Review highlights a shift to the “inference era,” where responsiveness and throughput win. Most enterprises react by buying more compute. In practice, I see latency and cost blown up by memory and storage choices, not model size.

My take: three levers consistently beat a new GPU order:

- Proximity: keep models next to the data they touch most; reduce cross-zone hops.
- Caching: cache hot prompts/embeddings and common tool outputs; avoid recomputing.
- Retrieval discipline: right-size context; prune tokens that don’t move decisions.

Track the right dials: p95 latency, tokens/sec/user, cache hit rate, and $/resolved ticket or $/successful action. If these don’t improve, hardware won’t save you.

One client cut p95 by 40% and cost per resolution by 28% without changing the model—just smarter data movement.

If you got surprise cloud overages last month, where’s your memory/storage heat map? #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #AIAdoption
